title: Helsinki EPIC Workshop develops three ideas for transnational cooperation on crisis preparedness
content:
On 23 September 2026, the third EPIC workshop brought together members of the NDPHS Occupational Safety and Health Expert Group (OSH EG) and invited experts in Helsinki to continue developing ideas for a future transnational project on workforce resilience and crisis preparedness. The overall workshop concept was developed jointly by the NDPHS Secretariat and Owe Österbacka, Chair of the OSH Expert Group.

The EPIC – “Effectively Prepared in Crisis” project, funded by the Swedish Institute, aims to enhance collaboration on health-related emergency preparedness and crisis response across the NDPHS Partner Countries and Ukraine, while sharing expertise, lessons learned and good practices to strengthen resilience during crises.

title: Programming for 2028-2034 happens now – and the Strategy is here to support!
content:
While we have 1.5 years left of the current EU programme period, the preparatory work for the post-2027 period is in full swing. Authorities are currently mapping the needs to enable the definition of the most relevant thematic focus areas for the funding programmes. The EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region Action Plan provides a solid starting point for the needs assessments.

Over the autumn of 2026, the Strategy Secretariat organises a series of thematic dialogues which bring together funding programmes and the thematic Coordinators of the Strategy. These meetings are the platform for the programme authorities in the region to come together and establish a shared understanding of common needs and challenges across the Baltic Sea Region. The aim is to facilitate cross-fertilisation with national programming processes and the preparation of National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs), including the Interreg Plan and Chapters.

The dialogues also contribute to building synergies among programmes and with Policy Area Coordinators, and lay the groundwork for joint implementation, including coordinated or synchronised calls.

title: Arts and mental health in wartime: Exchanging experiences with Ukraine
content:
How can arts and cultural activities support people living with trauma, grief, displacement and the continuing pressure of war? And what can mental health professionals across the Baltic Sea Region learn from the experience of Ukrainian communities?

These questions were at the heart of the third international meeting of the Arts for Health and Well-being Network (ArtWell NET), held in Kolomyia, Ukraine. Partners from Ukraine, Sweden, Poland and Estonia came together with local psychologists, educators and cultural professionals to exchange experience and explore how arts-based approaches can support mental health, recovery and community resilience.

For communities in Ukraine, mental health support is needed in circumstances of continuing uncertainty and loss. Veterans, military families, internally displaced people, children and professionals supporting others may all face the psychological consequences of war.

Clinical services remain essential, but they cannot meet every need alone. Safe group activities, trusted local networks and opportunities for creativity and connection can also help people regain a sense of belonging, express difficult emotions and rebuild everyday routines.

title: Policy Area Education joins discussion at the EU Week of Regions and Cities on supporting young people
content:
Policy Area Education Coordinator, Anders Bergström from Norden Association Sweden, will contribute as a speaker to a workshop on supporting vulnerable young people as they move from adolescence into adulthood during the European Week of Regions and Cities in Brussels on 14 October 2026.

The workshop, “No child left behind: building bridges to adulthood”, will examine what happens when young people move beyond child-focused services and encounter fragmented systems across education, employment, housing, health and social support.

Participants will discuss how local and regional actors can create more integrated and youth-friendly pathways through coordinated support, early guidance, tailored referrals and stronger cooperation across sectors and levels of governance. The discussion takes place in the context of the EU Anti-Poverty Strategy and the strengthened European Child Guarantee.

The workshop is part of the European Week of Regions and Cities, taking place in Brussels in October. EUSBSR is participating in several activities during the week, including its own discussions on macro-regional cooperation.

Read more about the workshop and register on the event page.

title: InnoCulture 2026: New Spaces for Culture — Registration is open
content:
What conditions does culture need to flourish? And how can culture create new spaces of its own?

Across the Baltic Sea Region, cultural and creative sectors are navigating rapid technological change, social fragmentation, and shifting political and financial priorities. To stay vibrant, culture needs new spaces in which to create, connect, and contribute.

For its 3rd edition, InnoCulture brings together cultural institutions, NGOs, policymakers, educators, and creative-sector leaders to explore how we build the ecosystems, opportunities, and conditions for culture and creativity to thrive.

Over two days in Hamburg, we’ll approach space on three levels:
→ Create space — the strategic conditions cities and regions can build for cultural work
→ Share space — culture as a driver of inclusion, participation, and democratic resilience
→ Secure space — stronger recognition and sustainable futures for culture in policy

Registration is open until 4th of November https://forms.gle/Bn8yzayG6WfWS8J59

Organised by Policy Area Culture, together with Hamburg Kreativ Gesellschaft, Ars Baltica, Baltic Sea Cultural Centre, and the Goethe-Institut CCI Contact Desk.

title: Why is the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region important for the civil society?
content:
More than 100 representatives of Danish civil society organisations took part, onsite and online, in a seminar at Europe House in Copenhagen on 2 September 2026 to discuss why the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR) matters and how civil society can contribute to its implementation.

The seminar was organised by the Danish Baltic Sea NGO Network, the Danish UN Association, the European Movement, the Norden Association Denmark, the European Commission Representation in Denmark and the Helsinki Committee for Human Rights.

Jens William Grav of the Danish Baltic Sea NGO Network welcomed participants and introduced the theme. The Baltic Sea Region faces major challenges that cross national borders, but it is also a region with strong traditions of transnational cooperation between democratic countries, municipalities, businesses, academic institutions and civil society.

title: Baltic Sea Region Cultural Pearls reaches the REGIOSTARS Awards 2026 finals
content:
The Public vote is open: Baltic Sea Region Cultural Pearls has been selected as a finalist for the REGIOSTARS Awards 2026 in Category 5, “A Europe Closer to the Citizens”.

Out of 270+ applications from across Europe, 25 projects were selected as finalists by the REGIOSTARS jury. BSR Cultural Pearls is one of them and now has the chance to compete for the REGIOSTARS People’s Choice Award, which will be decided by public vote.

What are the REGIOSTARS Awards?

Organised annually by the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Regional and Urban Policy (DG REGIO), the REGIOSTARS Awards celebrate outstanding EU-funded projects that demonstrate the impact of regional development and inspire other regions across Europe.

The public vote opens on 3 September 2026 and will run until 14 October 2026. Everyone can vote for their favourite finalist, and the project receiving the most votes will receive the People’s Choice Award.

How to vote for BSR Cultural Pearls:

  • Click the link: Inforegio – REGIOSTARS Awards
  • Select Category 5: A Europe Closer to the Citizens
  • Select “BSRCulturalPearls”
  • Confirm the vote

title: Registration open for Stockholm workshop on outreach work for young people in NEET situations
content:
Registration is now open for a combined workshop and study visit in Stockholm on 10–12 November 2026, organised by the Baltic Sea Network for Youth Guidance Centres and NEET Services.

The event will bring together network members to exchange experiences on how to identify, reach and motivate young people in NEET situations to seek support and take steps towards education or employment. The programme includes peer-learning workshops, presentations and study visits hosted in cooperation with the City of Stockholm.

Registration is open until 10 October 2026. Participation is limited to 50 people.

Read more and register on the event page.

title: Building stronger alliances for rural water management in the Baltic Sea Region
content:
How can countries around the Baltic Sea work together more effectively to improve water management from source to sea? This question brought together experts, projects and policy actors in Tallinn to share practical experiences and strengthen cooperation on catchment-based water management at an event called Focus on Clean Water Alliances.

Catchment-based water management is an important way to connect local action with wider environmental goals. By taking a holistic view of water management across an entire catchment area, it helps identify where measures are most needed, how they can be prioritised, and how local cooperation can support better results. Ann Riisenberg from the Estonian Ministry of Climate and Chair of EUSBSR Policy Area Nutri explains:

“The catchment-based approach is widely recognised as a key tool for holistic water governance and for implementing the source-to-sea concept within HELCOM and the EUSBSR. As practices and funding models vary between countries, there is a need to bring together experiences on a common platform.”

title: From enlargement to digitalisation: key outcomes from the 2026 EU Strategies Days
content:
This article is originally published on Panorama online magazine.

Cooperation is one of Europe’s key strengths, but it needs practice. Macro-regional and sea basin strategies provide that space, where candidate countries prepare for membership, regions work on shared challenges and young people gain experience in EU cooperation. At the Macro-Regional and Sea Basin Strategies Days 2026, this approach was reflected in discussions on enlargement, resilience, digital transformation and innovation.

The macro-regional and sea basin strategies are taking centre-stage in strengthening the EU’s resilience, supporting enlargement and helping regions respond to shared challenges. These were but some of the topics on the agenda at the Macro-Regional and Sea Basin Strategies Days 2026, which drew a 400-strong crowd of policymakers, regional authorities, partners and youth to Brussels in early July.

With Montenegro and Albania making progress in their accession negotiations, enlargement was high on the agenda. Discussions spotlighted how macro-regional cooperation gives candidate countries the chance to prepare for EU membership long before they officially join.
